_README: DEVELOPMENT ANNOTATIONS for the two sample videos.
The hackathon ships no ground truth for these videos, so this file is this
project's own annotation set. It is NOT ground truth and no metric computed
from it should be presented as a competition score.
* every interval was located by running the pipeline and then CONFIRMED by
looking at the video with scripts/inspect_rule_frame.py, which renders the
tracks, the signal colour read from the calibrated ROI, and each track's
front-bumper position relative to the stop line;
* the red_light intervals were additionally checked against the signal
phase timeline, and the supporting frame for the first one is committed
Coverage is PARTIAL and deliberately so. Only events a human actually
verified in the video are listed. An empty class means "no verified
instance was found", NOT "this class is absent from the video", so the
false-positive count measured against this file is an upper bound.
The most important negative finding is recorded explicitly: neither sample
video contains a visible collision, so `accident` is empty and the official
Part B score reduces to Score_A for this data.
